title: Privilege and confidentiality in generative AI workflows
abstract: arXiv:2607.05479v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) systems store and process client data in three distinct ways: in the model's parameters through training and memorisation, in the context window during a live session, and in knowledge databases for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Each mode creates different and often counter-intuitive risks to confidentiality and legal professional privilege, and each calls for specific governance responses. Drawing on the first English and American decisions to address privilege and generative AI, UK and Munir v Secretary of State for the Home Department and United States v Heppner, on the orthodox privilege authorities against which those decisions must be read, and on recent computer science research, we explain the three modes of data storage and processing in terms accessible to practitioners and analyse the legal consequences of each. translated_title: 生成式AI工作流中的特免权与保密性
translated_abstract: 生成式AI（GenAI）系统以三种不同的方式存储和处理客户数据：通过训练和记忆存储在模型参数中，在实时会话期间存储在上下文窗口中，以及存储在用于检索增强生成（RAG）的知识数据库中。每种模式都会对保密性和法律职业特免权造成不同且往往违反直觉的风险，并且每种模式都需要特定的治理应对措施。本文基于首批涉及特免权与生成式AI的英美判例——英国Munir诉内政大臣案和美国United States v Heppner案，基于解读这些判决所必须参照的正统特免权权威文献，以及近期的计算机科学研究，以从业者易于理解的方式解释了这三种数据存储和处理模式，并分析了每种模式的法律后果。随后，我们将这一分析置于规范律师执业的监管框架之中……
tldr: 本文结合首批英美判例与计算机科学研究，指出生成式AI通过模型参数、上下文窗口和RAG知识库三种模式存储客户数据，各自带来不同且违反直觉的保密性与法律职业特免权风险，需针对性地设计治理与法律应对措施。
en_tdlr: Drawing on the first English and American judicial decisions on privilege and generative AI, this paper shows that the three modes of client data storage in GenAI systems—model parameters, context windows, and RAG knowledge databases—each pose distinct and counter-intuitive risks to confidentiality and legal professional privilege, requiring tailored governance responses.
